newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two Frenchmen kill themselves in paedophile probe.
newsitem.headline: Two Frenchmen kill themselves in paedophile probe.

text.p: Two more men caught up in France's biggest ever crackdown on paedophiles have committed suicide, bringing to three the number of self-inflicted deaths in the case, police said on Friday.
The latest death was that of an unemployed, 37-year-old handicapped man, who killed himself in Givors, near Lyon, on Friday. His name was not released.
He had been detained during the police investigation but released for lack of evidence. The method he used to kill himself was not disclosed.
An unnamed 48-year-old bachelor, an executive at an arms factory in the central town of Tulle, hanged himself at his home on Thursday.

A postal inspector in his 40s was found hanged at his home in the eastern town of Saint-Martin-d'Heres also on Thursday after police questioned him about pornographic materials at his home. He had left a suicide note, police officials said.

The three were among more than 630 people rounded up this week across the country in a police operation that centred on clients of a mail-order company in the central town of Macon that allegedly sold pornographic films involving boys.
The man who committed suicide in Tulle was among 210 people formally placed under investigation on suspicion of "being in possession of images showing the corruption of minors aged under 15".
Of these, 18 have been remanded in custody, including the suspected ringleader, Bernard Alapetite, the 47-year-old head of a Paris publishing house.
Police said Alapetite copied foreign child sex videos and sold them for 800 francs ($140) each.

The operation -- dubbed "Ado 71" after the French word for teenager and the car registration figure for the Macon region -- involved about 2,500 gendarmes across mainland France as well as on the French Caribbean islands of Martinique and Guadeloupe.
